title: How to automate Claude safely with Zapier MCP
summary: Learn how to install Zapier MCP and let Claude Chat and Code act across your favorite apps.
body_markdown:
I've been playing this game at coffee shops where every time I overhear somebody say they're "building with AI," I take a sip of my cold brew. Suffice it to say, I'm staying caffeinated (and staying up at night).


Your IT admins may be losing sleep too, if everyone's handing AI tools like Claude access to their work apps, giving it more chances to do something it shouldn't. Zapier MCP closes that gap, connecting Claude to your tech stack with governance built in. That way, your AI can take only the actions you allow.


Below, I'll show you how to install Zapier MCP in Claude—whether you prefer to work in Chat or Code—and share a few templates to get you started fast. I'll also show you how Claude can turn repeat work into an automation that Zapier runs for you, starting whenever something happens in your apps. Claude does the building, and Zapier keeps it running.


**Note:** The templates in this post work with any AI tool that supports MCP, not just Claude.

## What is Zapier MCP?


[Zapier MCP](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-mcp-guide/) is a tool you install in your AI to connect it to your other apps. It's for when you want to go beyond prompting and have AI carry out work for you. For example, instead of just asking Claude to write you an email that you'll send to your vendor list, maybe you want it to reach into your CRM, pull the names and addresses for a group of vendors, and create a draft in Gmail without navigating away from your Claude window. That's the kind of thing Zapier MCP makes possible.


AI tools come with native[connectors](https://zapier.com/blog/claude-connectors/) of their own. But Zapier MCP is different because you decide exactly what Claude can do. You install it once with a few clicks, then give it access to just the apps and actions you allow. If you want Claude to draft a reply but never to send one, setting that up is easy. So is making sure it can never delete any records in your apps. And you can revoke access to an app or action anytime your needs change.


Claude's built-in connectors cover the basics, like looking up a record or updating a field. Zapier goes deeper, so Claude can do things like convert a lead in Salesforce or enroll a contact in a HubSpot nurture sequence, across 10,000+


apps. You connect your accounts once, and the same connections work from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any other AI tool that supports MCP, so switching tools doesn't mean starting over.


I've heard people claim that AI won't do anything you don't want it to, as long as you give it the right instructions. That reminds me of a favorite phrase of my brother-in-law: "I pretty much guarantee it." When everyone at your company is tinkering with AI, you need more than a "pretty-much guarantee" that it won't leak credentials or take some other improper action. You need the security Zapier MCP provides.


## Should I use Zapier MCP with Claude Chat or Claude Code?


Once you've decided Claude should act on your apps within limits you set, the next question is where to install Zapier MCP. If you're working in Claude, your options are Claude Chat, Claude Code, or some mix of the two.


To help you decide, here's a rundown of what Zapier MCP unlocks in each.


**Pro tip:** Not sure which Claude model to use for your workflows? Our[guide to AI models on Zapier](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-models-on-zapier/) covers every model available from Anthropic, OpenAI, and other providers.


### Claude Chat


Chat is the surface most people mean when they just say "Claude." It's a chat interface, but it can also work with the files on your computer, use your apps, and run code (this part used to be called Claude Cowork). It can even control your screen directly by clicking, typing, and navigating on its own. Plus, it lets you build tasks that run on a schedule.


With Zapier MCP installed, you can request one-off actions in your other apps without ever leaving your Claude conversation. This means you can build more complex workflows while retaining control over exactly which apps and actions Claude can touch.


**Note:** Claude can run scheduled tasks, but only while your computer is on and the desktop app is open. Once you close the app, the session stops. These are time-based automations, too, not event-based ones. If you want a workflow to run whether your computer is open or not, or to fire from an event-based trigger, build a Zap instead, and ask Claude to draft it for you through Zapier MCP. A Zap can start when something happens in an app or on a schedule, so it keeps working with your laptop closed. You can still use AI in a Zap workflow: add AI steps from your preferred model with our built-in tool,[AI by Zapier](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-by-zapier-guide/) , and let regular steps handle the rest.


### Claude Code


Claude Code is an AI coding assistant. It's built to understand and act on a codebase specifically—tracing logic across files, working directly with git, running tests, and opening pull requests. It works wherever you write software, whether that's the terminal, your IDE, the desktop app, or your phone.


Install Zapier MCP into Claude Code, and you get conversational access to your apps right alongside your code. So you can say "post this to Slack" or "grab my open Jira tickets" mid-task without switching tools. And as with Chat, you can build time-based automations.


Claude Code also comes with another option: You can[install the Zapier SDK](https://zapier.com/sdk) here instead of Zapier MCP. The SDK is a set of building blocks for wiring Zapier's actions straight into your code, so when you need loops, error handling, multi-app chains, or something that runs autonomously in the background, you've got full programmatic control.


So which do you pick? It comes down to what you're making. Using Zapier MCP with Claude Code is best when the action is the end goal: you want something done right now, inside the conversation, and then you move on. The SDK is best when the code is the end goal, when you're building something that outlives the conversation, runs on its own schedule, and can be refined over time.


## How to install Zapier MCP in Claude


Before you try the workflows below, you'll need to install Zapier MCP into Claude if you haven't already. If you can click, type, and copy-paste, you can set this up in minutes. Just follow these steps:


1.


Head to the[Zapier MCP dashboard](http://mcp.zapier.com/) .


2.


Click **+New MCP Server** and choose **Claude** or **Claude Code** as the client.


3.


Now set up your first action. Click **+Add tool** .


4.


Search for the app you want to connect to, then click **its corresponding** **tile** .


5.


Select whichever action events you want to connect, then click **Connect** .


6.


Connect your app accounts as needed.


7.


In the dashboard, configure each action according to your needs by clicking the kebab menu (⋮) and then **Configure** and adjusting values as needed. Hover over the tooltip icons next to any field for more details. When you're done, click **Save** .


8.


Finally, click **Connect** at the top of the MCP dashboard and follow the instructions to add this server to your Claude account.


## 5 ways to automate Claude with Zapier MCP


### Schedule and prepare for meetings


You're an EA scheduling meetings—or you manage your own busy calendar—and you want a faster way to find open times and show up to meetings prepared.


Schedule meetings with email context


Find open calendar slots, create a Google Meet invite, and pull recent email history to prep for your meeting


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/schedule-meetings-with-email-context)


### Update your CRM and ticketing tool


You're a sales rep or support agent who wants to delegate data entry, so you can reserve your energy and focus for the actual conversations you're having. Logging calls, updating records, and writing follow-ups should happen automatically.


Log calls and update CRM automatically


Update Salesforce, create a Zendesk ticket, and draft a follow-up email after every call


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/log-calls-and-update-crm-automatically)


### Repurpose and distribute content


You're a marketing team member who needs to repurpose a finished piece across multiple channels, and you want the distribution work done before you exit your Claude tab.


Repurpose blog content across channels


Turn a blog post into scheduled social posts and an email draft, all aligned with your brand guidelines


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/repurpose-blog-content-across-channels)


### Pull data and draft reports


You're in ops or finance, and you produce a recurring report that requires pulling numbers from multiple places, spotting what changed, and writing a narrative around it. You want Claude to do the legwork.


Generate weekly reports from multiple sources


Pull data from Google Sheets and Looker, flag anomalies, and write a summary to your Google Doc template


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/generate-weekly-reports-from-multiple-sources)


### Classify and route messages at scale


You manage a high-volume inbox or shared queue and need a faster way to know what actually needs whose attention—without reading everything yourself.


Triage inbox and route messages automatically


Prioritize emails and Slack messages, summarize them, and route to the right channel or create Jira tickets


[Try it](https://zapier.com/templates/details/triage-inbox-and-route-messages-automatically)


### Turn what you repeat into a Zap


Most of the examples above start as a one-off request. The ones worth keeping are the ones you end up repeating. When that happens, ask Claude to build a Zap instead of running the task by hand again. For example: "Whenever a Zendesk ticket is marked urgent, summarize it, look up the customer in Salesforce, and post it to #support-escalations in Slack." Claude drafts the Zap and deploys it to Zapier, where it starts on the real event, a new urgent ticket in this case, instead of waiting for you to ask.


Three things keep it dependable once it's running:


-


**The same result every time.** Zaps use AI only in the steps that call for judgment, like summarizing the ticket. Everything else is a regular step, which runs faster and costs less, so Monday's run looks like Friday's.


-


**Fixes for what breaks.** Zapier logs every run. When one fails, it tracks down the problem and proposes a fix you can approve, or you can work through it with Claude.


-


**Cheaper and steadier over time.** If an AI step ends up doing the same thing on every run, Zapier can offer to swap it for a regular step: same result, fewer tokens.


## Claude and Zapier MCP FAQ


### Why use Zapier if I already have Claude?


Keep Claude. Zapier adds 10,000+


apps, and when a job repeats, Claude can turn it into an automation that Zapier keeps running after the chat ends.


### Can't Claude's scheduled tasks do this?


Partly. A scheduled task runs at a set time, only while your computer is on and the Claude desktop app is open, and the model works through every step on every run. A Zap starts when something happens, like a new lead or ticket (or on a schedule, if you'd rather), runs whether your laptop is open or not, and uses AI only in the steps that need it. That makes the results steadier and the bill smaller.


### Why not have Claude Code write me a script?


You can, and the first version will probably work. The trouble starts later. A script needs somewhere to run, a way to hear about events, and someone to notice when it stops. When an API changes or a login expires, it fails quietly, and it often holds your keys on a laptop or in a repo. With Zapier, Claude builds the Zap, Zapier hosts it and starts it on real triggers, and each app's login is handled for you. When something breaks, Zapier finds the problem and proposes the fix. If you do want code, the Zapier SDK is there too.


### How do I connect Zapier to Claude via MCP?


Create a server in the Zapier MCP dashboard, choose Claude or Claude Code as the client, add the apps and actions you want to allow, and follow the connect instructions to add the server to your Claude account. The full steps are in the install section above. Once it's connected, Claude can run those actions from the conversation, and if it's work you'll repeat, it can turn it into a Zap.


## The safest way to give Claude access to your apps


The more that people build with AI across a company, the more security risks come with it. Every new app connection gives AI the chance to reach into something it shouldn't and go haywire.


That's why what Claude can access matters as much as what it can do. With Zapier MCP, Claude gets access to your apps, not your keys, and you decide what it can touch, what stays off limits, and when to turn access off. Whether you're asking Claude for a one-off task or having it build something that runs on its own, Zapier is where the work keeps running.
